docRequirement: plugins/host-marketplace.md#depend-on-and-recommend-other-plugins (was line 11 of the retired plugin-dependencies page) — "When you install a plugin that declares dependencies, Claude Code resolves and installs them automatically and lists which dependencies were added at the end of the install output." The acquisition rule is :108-:127: version constraints resolve against git tags named `{plugin-name}--v{version}` on the marketplace repository, and on install Claude Code "lists the marketplace's tags, filters to those starting with `secrets-vault--v`, and fetches the highest version satisfying `~2.1.0`" (:127); :45 — "The dependency is fetched at the highest tagged version that satisfies this range"; :215 — no such tag is the `no-matching-tag` error. :52-:70 makes the bundle pattern (a manifest that is only `name` + `dependencies`) a supported way to ship a curated plugin set behind one install.
current: The `dependencies` array is parsed, merged and carried correctly, and every LOAD-TIME consequence of the page is built — but nothing is ever fetched. (1) Install has no dependency step: `PluginManagementServiceV2.installUnlocked` (packages/shared/src/plugins/management-service-v2.ts:132-203) materializes one bundle, commits it at :165, optionally activates it at :180, and returns; `installed.manifest.dependencies` is never read there. `PluginManagementInstallResult` (packages/shared/src/plugins/management-types.ts:137-149) has no field for "which dependencies were added", so :11's install output cannot exist. (2) No tag enumeration anywhere: `grep -a` for `--v`, `git tag`, `ls-remote`, `refs/tags` across packages/shared/src, packages/server-core/src and apps/cli/src returns zero hits in the plugin path. Repository installs are HTTP archive downloads at a pinned ref — `fetchRepositoryArtifact` (packages/shared/src/plugins/install-service.ts:826-874) calls `repositoryArchiveUrl(spec, ref)` (:1736-1746) with `spec.ref` or `fetchRepositoryDefaultRef` (:1259-1265); there is no git binary and no tag route. (3) The absence is deliberate and recorded: packages/shared/src/plugins/dependencies.ts:15-23 and packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1575-1589 both state that no marketplace source enumerates `{plugin-name}--v{version}` tags, so resolving a range against "whatever the catalog currently holds" would make `~2.1.0` silently mean latest. (4) It is surfaced, not silent: `normalizeClaudeDependencies` pushes a `dependency-auto-install` deferred record for any manifest that declares dependencies (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1608-1613, reasonCode `plugin.deferred.claude_dependency_auto_install`). (5) The `version` range is used only as a post-hoc check: `resolvePluginDependencyErrors` (packages/shared/src/plugins/dependencies.ts:68-141) calls `satisfies(resolved.version, dependency.version, { includePrerelease: false })` at :122-:131 against whatever is ALREADY installed, and a dependency that is absent or disabled yields `dependency-unsatisfied` at :100-:116. (6) That verdict is enforced: packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:1703-1707 sets `enabled = false` with `unavailableReason` = the error code on EVERY capability of the dependent plugin, fed by `resolveActiveDependencyErrors` (resolver.ts:1581, :2145-2158); apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:419-459 runs the same function so `plugin list --json` cannot disagree. (7) Enable/disable graph handling IS built for already-installed plugins: `resolveTransitiveDependencies` (management-service-v2.ts:694-728) enables the closure or throws `plugin.manage.dependency-not-installed`, and `assertNoEnabledDependents` (:740-772) refuses a disable with the chained command. (8) `no-matching-tag` does not exist as a code: the union is the other three at packages/shared/src/plugins/dependencies.ts:36 and at the wire projection packages/shared/src/protocol/capabilities.ts:313-320. (9) `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` appears in no source file — `grep -a` finds it only in vendored Pi/session-mcp bundles and in plan prose; claude.ts:1582-1589 records that it is not carried past catalog parse.
divergence: Not a key-name or value mismatch — the manifest key, the shapes (`"audit-logger"` and `{ name, version, marketplace }` → `PluginDependencyDescriptor`, packages/shared/src/plugins/types.ts:708-713) and every load-time rule the page states are correct. What is absent is the ACQUISITION half, in two independent pieces. (a) Install-time resolution: `installUnlocked` never looks at `manifest.dependencies`, so installing a plugin installs exactly one plugin and the install result has no dependency list — the documented bundle pattern (:52-:70, "Installing `backend-standard` resolves and installs all four dependencies") installs zero of the four. (b) Tag-based version selection: nothing lists `{plugin-name}--v{version}` tags, so `version` can only ever be an after-the-fact verdict on an already-present install, never a selector for which version to fetch. Net effect on a declared `~2.1.0`: it can disable a plugin but can never satisfy one. Four page behaviours fall out of the same root: range intersection across dependents and its install-time `range-conflict` (:142-:148), the cross-marketplace refusal and `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` (:81, :104), `--prune` of orphaned auto-installed dependencies and the provenance bit it needs (:180-:198), and the `no-matching-tag` error (:215).

change.symbol: fetchRepositoryTags (new, beside fetchRepositoryDefaultRef:1259) + pluginVersionTags/resolvePluginTagForRange (new module-level helpers beside repositoryArchiveUrl:1736)
change.what: Add HTTP tag enumeration — the one missing prerequisite, and it is smaller than the plans assume: `repositoryApiUrl(spec)` (:1711-1716) already yields `https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}` and the GitLab `/api/v4/projects/{id}` base, and both hosts expose tags on that base (`/tags` for GitHub, `/repository/tags` for GitLab). Fetch through the existing `this.artifactAuthProvider.fetchArtifact(url, this.fetchImpl)` exactly as `fetchRepositoryDefaultRef` does; paginate `per_page=100`; return `{ name, commitSha }[]`. Then `pluginVersionTags(tags, pluginName)` filters to `name.startsWith(`${pluginName}--v`)` — a prefix match on the FULL plugin name, which is :125's rule for hyphenated names — and parses the suffix as semver. `resolvePluginTagForRange(tags, pluginName, range)` returns the highest satisfying entry with `{ includePrerelease: false }` (:48), or a `no-matching-tag` result carrying the available versions (:127, :215). No git binary; no new egress host beyond the ones already contacted.

After the successful `this.store.install(...)` at :165, resolve `installed.manifest.dependencies` and install what is missing before the activation block at :180. Resolve each dependency's install source by (marketplaceId, pluginName) through the marketplace catalog items layer; where that source is a `repository`, pick the ref from `resolvePluginTagForRange`. Recurse over the installed dependency's own dependencies with the visited-set/queue shape already proven in `resolveTransitiveDependencies` (:694-728) so a cycle terminates. Write explicit `true` activation for each dependency at the same target (:167 — the explicit `true` outranks a dependency's own `defaultEnabled: false`). Refuse a dependency whose `marketplace` differs from the root marketplace unless that name is in the root marketplace's `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn`, with a `cross-marketplace` diagnostic naming the field (:81, :104). Intersect all installed dependents' ranges before choosing a tag and fail the install with `range-conflict` when the intersection is empty (:142-:148). Return the added set.

Add `installedDependencies?: Array<{ pluginKey: PluginKey; version: string; tag?: string }>` so :11's "lists which dependencies were added at the end of the install output" has a value to print. Add the two new diagnostic codes (`plugin.install.cross_marketplace_dependency`, `plugin.install.no_matching_tag`).

Persist an auto-install provenance bit on records created by the dependency step. This is what `--prune` needs (:196 — "Plugins you installed yourself are never pruned, only those installed automatically through another plugin's `dependencies` array"). PERSISTED STORE CHANGE: needs a default for records written before it and a read path that treats absent as user-installed.

blastRadius: `resolvePluginDependencyErrors` (packages/shared/src/plugins/dependencies.ts:68) has exactly two production callers — `resolveActiveDependencyErrors` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:2145, called at :1581) and apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:424 — and its verdict disables every capability of the dependent plugin at resolver.ts:1703-1707, so a resolution change flips whole plugins on or off, not a badge. WIRE BOUNDARY: `dependencyErrors` is projected to the renderer through packages/shared/src/protocol/capabilities.ts:313-320; widening the code union is a wire change and a risk trigger in this repo. PERSISTENCE BOUNDARY: the auto-install provenance bit lands in the installed registry (packages/shared/src/plugins/store-v2.ts) and must default safely for pre-existing records. NETWORK: a new REST route (`/tags`, `/repository/tags`) through `artifactAuthProvider.fetchArtifact` — same hosts as `fetchRepositoryDefaultRef` (install-service.ts:1259) but a new endpoint, so corporate-proxy and auth behaviour must be re-checked. Install becomes recursive and network-bound, which changes the failure surface of every `plugins.install` RPC caller and of `update`/`repair` (management-service-v2.ts:515, :522, :579), all of which share `PluginManagementInstallResult`. IMPORTED-PLUGIN PATHS: the Claude adapter's dependency normalization (format-adapters/claude.ts:1591) and marketplace-entry merge (:1598-:1606) feed the same descriptors; the Codex adapter declares no dependencies, so this is Claude-only input. TESTS: packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/resolver.test.ts:1383-1490 (four dependency-unsatisfied assertions), packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/management-service-v2.test.ts:1052 (transitive enable), packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/format-adapters.test.ts:2721 (the deferred record). `resolvePluginDependencyErrors` itself has no direct unit test — codegraph reports no covering tests for it; the coverage is indirect through the resolver suite.
userImpact: None observable against the official Claude catalogue today. Measured 2026-08-02: 0 of the 276 entries in `anthropics/claude-plugins-official`'s `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` carry a `dependencies` key (the union of entry keys is author/category/description/displayName/homepage/keywords/lspServers/name/skills/source/strict/tags/version), and 0 of the 74 per-plugin `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifests fetched at their pinned shas from the 81 git-subdir/github entries declare one. It surfaces the first time a team points Nessy at an internal marketplace that uses the documented bundle pattern (:52-:70): the user runs one install of `backend-standard`, Sources shows it installed, and it does nothing — because its manifest is only a `dependencies` array, none of its four plugins is present, `resolveActiveDependencyErrors` marks it `dependency-unsatisfied`, and resolver.ts:1703-1707 disables every capability it has. The visible text is dependencies.ts:151, "This plugin requires <name>, which is not installed or is disabled. Install it, or enable it if it is already installed.", repeated per dependency, and the same list appears under `errors` in `nessy-general-agent plugin list --json`. A constrained dependency behaves the same even when the user installs it by hand: if the version they happen to get is outside the range they get `dependency-version-unsatisfied` (dependencies.ts:122-131) with no way for Nessy to fetch the matching tag. The workaround — install each dependency manually, which :104 itself blesses — works; what is missing is the one-install-for-a-curated-set promise the page is written around.
notes: Read in full: the doc page (224 lines, curl -sL, not WebFetch); packages/shared/src/plugins/dependencies.ts (whole file); types.ts:680-739; format-adapters/claude.ts:1540-1629; management-service-v2.ts:100-269 and :660-780; capabilities/resolver.ts:1570-1609, :1685-1724, :2138-2182; apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:400-459; protocol/capabilities.ts:300-330; install-service.ts:824-875, :1259-1265, :1711-1746; management-types.ts:137-185; docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-plugin-dependencies-and-monitors.md:188-263. Absence claims used `grep -a` throughout (several files here carry a NUL byte). Sibling-subsystem trap checked: install-service.ts's ~40 `dependenc*` hits are npm RUNTIME dependencies of executable plugins (lockfiles, quotas, `plugin.install.runtime_dependency_*`) and packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/plugin-runtime-dependencies.ts is the bun installer — a different subsystem from plugin-to-plugin manifest `dependencies`; this spec is about the latter only. TWO THINGS I DID NOT VERIFY. (1) The impact sample is partial: 74 of 276 official manifests, all from git-subdir/github entries; the 142 `url`-source and 53 bare-string entries were not probed, so a dependency-declaring official plugin could exist among them — that would raise userImpact from 'none observable' to 'observable on the official catalogue'. (2) I did not execute a tag request, so I have not proven `api.github.com/repos/{o}/{r}/tags` and the GitLab `/repository/tags` route are reachable through this environment's proxy in a packaged build; the claim that the route is available is from `repositoryApiUrl` (install-service.ts:1711-1716) already using the same API bases, not from a live call. NUANCE WORTH CARRYING: dependencies.ts:17-23, claude.ts:1575-1581 and the plan at :206-:210 all describe the prerequisite as 'a git-network capability that does not exist anywhere in this repo'. That framing is true of the code as written but overstates the cost — the repo never needed git, only two REST paths hanging off a base URL it already computes, so this is a bounded HTTP addition rather than a new subsystem. The tag-vs-catalog reasoning behind the deferral still stands and should be preserved as the rule the new code implements, not discarded.
